old: Six counts each carbon as its own signal. Equivalent carbons (the two isopropyl CH<sub>3</sub>) give one signal, and the ethyl and OCH carbons each carry one set.
new: Six is more signals than there are carbons bearing H (five). The two isopropyl CH<sub>3</sub> groups are equivalent, so there are only four sets of H.
why: Ethyl isopropyl ether has 5 carbons, so "six counts each carbon" is false

old: Six counts carbons, not sets of equivalent hydrogens; the two methyls are one set.
new: Six is more signals than the molecule has carbons (five). The two CH<sub>3</sub> groups on the same CH are one set, so there are only four sets of H.
why: 1-Bromo-3-methylbutane has 5 carbons, so "six counts carbons" is false

old: This treats Cl as if it did not count. A halogen takes the place of an H, so it is subtracted like H.
new: This adds the Cl to the allowed H count instead of subtracting it. A halogen takes the place of an H, so it is subtracted like H.
why: Ignoring Cl gives (18+2+1-10)/2 = 5.5, not 6; adding Cl gives (18+2+1-10+1)/2 = 6

old: The odd electron of a vinylic radical sits in an sp<sup>2</sup> orbital in the plane of the π bond, so it is not delocalized; vinylic radicals are very unstable.
new: The odd electron of a vinylic radical sits in an sp<sup>2</sup> orbital perpendicular to the π orbitals, so it is not delocalized; vinylic radicals are very unstable.
why: The sp2 orbital lies in the nodal plane of the π bond, orthogonal to it; "in the plane of the π bond" is misleading
